metadata.note: The Frisco's Memphis-Birmingham main line through Tupelo -- the east-west half of the railroad crossing that created the town. The Kansas City, Memphis and Birmingham, incorporated in Mississippi on Feb 18 1886, took over the unfinished Memphis, Birmingham and Atlantic and completed the line from Holly Springs through Tupelo to Birmingham in 1887; the Frisco absorbed it operationally in 1896. Into the late 1950s it still brought the Kansas City-Florida Special, the Memphian and the Sunnyland through Tupelo. The Southland's last run on Dec 9 1967 ended passenger service across the whole of northeast Mississippi. See mobile_and_ohio_tupelo.geojson for the north-south line that crossed it.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Memphis_and_Birmingham_Railroad (incorporated in Mississippi Feb 18 1886, consolidated 1887 with the Memphis and Birmingham Railway; main line Memphis to Birmingham completed 1887, about 276 miles; merged into the Frisco Sep 1 1928)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tupelo,_Mississippi (the KCM&B acquired the unfinished Memphis, Birmingham and Atlantic and completed the line from Holly Springs through Tupelo to Birmingham; operationally absorbed into the Frisco in 1896; the Frisco's Southland ceased running Dec 9 1967, marking the last passenger train in northeast Mississippi)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis%E2%80%93San_Francisco_Railway (the Frisco operated 1876 to Nov 21 1980, when it merged into the Burlington Northern; the Sunnyland among its named trains)

Named trains serving Tupelo into the late 1950s -- the Kansas City-Florida Special, Memphian and Sunnyland -- are from secondary summaries of Frisco passenger service and have not been checked against a timetable
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Headways are estimates and no timetable has been consulted. The 1958 segment boundary is not a documented event: the only anchor is that these trains served Tupelo 'into the late 1950s', so 1958 marks that bound rather than a dated change. Individual end dates for the Kansas City-Florida Special, Memphian and Sunnyland at Tupelo are unknown; only the Southland's Dec 9 1967 finale is dated. The traced length is 235 mi against a documented 276.

segments.note: The KCM&B was operationally absorbed into the St. Louis and San Francisco Railway -- the Frisco -- in 1896, the corporate merger following on Sep 1 1928. Into the late 1950s Tupelo was still served by the Frisco's Kansas City-Florida Special (Kansas City - Memphis - Jacksonville), the Memphian (Memphis - Birmingham) and the Sunnyland, which ran west to Kansas City with sections east to Birmingham and Pensacola. segments.note: The last years, down to a single train. The Frisco's Southland made its final run on Dec 9 1967 -- the last passenger train not just at Tupelo but in the whole of northeast Mississippi. The Frisco itself merged into the Burlington Northern on Nov 21 1980 and the line is BNSF freight today. Frequency estimated/unsourced
